children: Oil futures are sharply higher with WTI hitting $100 a barrel for the first time since May amid increased military strikes between the U.S. and Iran and Houthi advances toward the Bab el-Mandeb strait. "The move is raising fresh concerns about the security of global energy supplies," Fawad Razaqzada of Forex.com says in a note. "A sustained move above $100 in WTI would put renewed upward pressure on inflation expectations." WTI is up 4.1% at $99.95 a barrel and Brent is 3.8% higher at $105.10 a barrel. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
